knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A cracked heater is a shock and overheating hazard. It is unplugged, taken out of service and replaced, and taping it is wrong.
A drip loop makes water run off the cord rather than down it into the outlet. It does not affect the pump's noise or the water temperature.
Wiring and repair of a mains connection is electrical work and is licensed in many circumstances. Completing this lesson does not give that authority.

practicalCriteria: Learner isolates a heater and a pump on a training set-up, and proves each one off before handling it
Learner identifies a cracked heater and a damaged cord on a training set, takes both out of service, and labels them
Learner forms a drip loop on a training cord, and explains in one sentence how it protects the outlet
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Isolation record for the training set-up
Inspection record with items taken out of service and their labels
Electrical referral note for the fault
Assessor observation of isolation and inspection
stopWorkCriteria: Any work on a connection while the equipment is still plugged in
A request to tape or repair a damaged heater or cord
Any wiring, controller or fixed lighting work by a person without a licence
